text.p: Belgian biotechnology firm Innogenetics NV, which is listed on the small cap market Easdaq, said on Wednesday turnover climbed to 829.8 million Belgian francs in 1996, up 54 percent from 538.8 million in 1995.
"The increases were mainly due to sales of Innogenetics niche products, especially the rapidly developing market segment of DNA diagnostics," CEO Hugo Van Heuverswyn said in a statement.
The company said product sales increased by 29.8 percent to 486.3 million francs in 1996, from 377.6 million francs in 1995.
"(The increase was) primarily due to a higher demand for the company's products in the areas of transplantation and genotyping," Innogenetics said.
Net income for 1996 was 51.8 million francs, compared to a net loss of 114.4 million in 1995.

"In a very competitive world-wide diagnostics market, Innogenetics succeeded in significantly increasing its market share in diagnostic products and recorded a substantial sales increase," Van Heuverswyn said.

Contract revenues increased to 47.8 million francs, compared to 20.9 million in 1995, primarily as a result of the infectious diseases collaboration with German pharmaceutical giant Boehringer Mannheim.
"Growth was evenly divided over the various continents and markets, with noticeable progress in Italy, Spain, France, Germany and Japan," Van Heuverswyn said.
Innogenetics, which sells diagnostic tests for diseases such as HIV and Alzheimers, targets five disease areas: infectious diseases, tissue repair, immune and neurodegenerative and genetic disorders.
